title: What JSX Is
summary: JSX is function calls: build a tiny createElement and renderer to see how.

steps.title: JSX compiles to function calls
body: JSX looks like HTML inside TypeScript, but it is **syntax for function calls**. The compiler turns this:
and the result is a plain object describing the element:
- It uses `className` and `htmlFor`, because `class` and `for` are JavaScript keywords.
- `{ ... }` holds any **expression** (not statements), so you use `map`, `&&` and ternaries, not `for` and `if`.
- A component name must start with a **capital letter**: `<Card />` calls your `Card` function; `<card />` would mean an HTML tag.
- A component returns **one** root (use `<>...</>`, a Fragment, to group without a wrapper).

steps.prompt: Match the JSX to its plain-object meaning.
Which is valid inside JSX braces `{ ... }`?
steps.explain: Braces take an expression. `&&`, `?:` and `map` are expressions; `if`, `for` and declarations are statements.

steps.title: Our own tiny renderer
body: You can build the core of JSX rendering in a few lines. An element is `{ type, props, children }`; a `type` is either a tag name or a component function.
type Child = VNode | string | number | false | null | undefined;
type VNode = { type: string | ((props: any) => VNode); props: Record<string, unknown>; children: Child[] };
const h = (type: VNode["type"], props: Record<string, unknown> | null, ...children: Child[]): VNode =>

`h` is the historic name (from "hyperscript"); React's version is `createElement`. Rendering walks the tree: strings are escaped text, `false`/`null`/`undefined` render nothing (that is why `{cond && <X />}` works), functions are called with their props to get more tree.

code: console.log(parts.map(p => (p === false || p === null || p === undefined ? "(nothing)" : JSON.stringify(p))).join(" "));
steps.explain: React renders nothing for `false`, `null` and `undefined`, but **does** render `0`. That is why `{items.length && <List />}` shows a stray `0`; write `{items.length > 0 && <List />}`.

steps.title: Render a VNode tree
prompt: Write `render(node: Child): string` turning the tree into HTML:
- strings and numbers render as escaped text
- if `type` is a function, call it with `{ ...props, children }` and render the result

- otherwise render `<type attrs>children</type>`; attributes come from `props` in order: `className` becomes `class`, `true` renders just the name (`disabled`), `false`/`null`/`undefined` are skipped, other values are escaped inside double quotes
starter: type Child = VNode | string | number | false | null | undefined;
type VNode = { type: string | ((props: any) => Child); props: Record<string, unknown>; children: Child[] };
const h = (type: VNode["type"], props: Record<string, unknown> | null, ...children: Child[]): VNode => ({ type, props: props ?? {}, children });
solution: function escapeHtml(s: string): string {
return s.replaceAll("&", "&").replaceAll("<", "<").replaceAll(">", ">").replaceAll('"', """).replaceAll("'", "'");
type Child = VNode | string | number | false | null | undefined;
type VNode = { type: string | ((props: any) => Child); props: Record<string, unknown>; children: Child[] };
const h = (type: VNode["type"], props: Record<string, unknown> | null, ...children: Child[]): VNode => ({ type, props: props ?? {}, children });
function render(node: Child): string {
if (node === false || node === null || node === undefined) return "";
if (typeof node === "string" || typeof node === "number") return escapeHtml(String(node));
if (typeof node.type === "function") return render(node.type({ ...node.props, children: node.children }));
const attrs = Object.entries(node.props)
.filter(([, v]) => v !== false && v !== null && v !== undefined)
const name = k === "className" ? "class" : k;
return v === true ? ` ${name}` : ` ${name}="${escapeHtml(String(v))}"`;
.join("");
return `<${node.type}${attrs}>${node.children.map(render).join("")}</${node.type}>`;

Dojo.eq("element with attributes", 'go', render(h("a", { className: "link", href: "/x?a=1&b=2" }, "go")));
Dojo.eq("boolean attributes", "<button disabled>Save</button>", render(h("button", { disabled: true, hidden: false }, "Save")));

const DojoBadge = ({ n }: { n: number }) => n > 0 && h("span", { className: "badge" }, n);
const DojoItem = ({ label, children }: { label: string; children: Child[] }) => h("li", null, label, ...children);

Dojo.eq("components", '
  • Inbox3

', render(h("ul", null, h(DojoItem, { label: "Inbox" }, h(DojoBadge, { n: 3 })), h(DojoItem, { label: "Spam" }, h(DojoBadge, { n: 0 })))));

steps.title: Write components for the renderer
prompt: - `Alert({ kind, children })` returning `h("div", { className: "alert alert-" + kind, role: "alert" }, ...children)`

- `TodoList({ todos })` returning a `ul` of `li`s; each `li` has `className: "done"` only when done (otherwise no class attribute at all: use `undefined`); when `todos` is empty return an `Alert` with kind `"info"` and the text `"All done!"`
